prompt:
You are generating a squash commit message for a feature branch.
Output in English only - all code, comments, commits, docs.

CONTEXT:
- Feature branch: feature/CC-0114
- Target branch: main
- Feature ID: CC-0114
- Feature title: Seed K-ORC bootstrap clouds.yaml from operator


YOUR TASK:
1. Run `git diff main...feature/CC-0114 -- . ':(exclude).planwerk/**'`
   to see ALL real code/feature changes (planning/status files are excluded)
2. Run `git log main..feature/CC-0114 --oneline -- . ':(exclude).planwerk/**'`
   to understand the commit history of the actual changes
3. Analyze the changes HOLISTICALLY — this will become ONE single commit

IMPORTANT RULES:
- Describe the FINAL STATE of the feature, not the journey (no "fix after review", etc.)
- The `.planwerk/` directory (status JSONs, reviews, feature files) is already
  excluded by the pathspec above — never mention it in the message
- IGNORE planning-system commits entirely: any `plan(...)`, `review(...)`, and any
  `chore(...)` whose subject is about reviews, feature status, or planning bookkeeping
- Focus ONLY on the actual code/feature changes that the feature introduces
- If initial implementation + later fixes exist, describe only the END RESULT
- NEVER mention fixes that only repair a bug introduced earlier in THIS SAME branch
  (e.g. "fix typo from previous commit", "correct regression from earlier commit").
  In the squashed end state that bug never existed, so the fix is not a real change —
  just describe the correct final code as if it had always been written that way
- DO include additional features/improvements that go BEYOND THE ORIGINAL feature
  scope (things discovered and completed during manual review/testing, not part of
  the initial plan). These are real changes in the end state — list them and mark
  them explicitly as additional so they are not lost (see the "Additionally" group
  in the FORMAT section)
- No contradictions — present it as one coherent feature delivery


<commit-best-practices>
<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"feat(CC-0114): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>

<git-identity>
  <rule name="author">ALWAYS use --author flag: git commit --author "Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>" -m "..."</rule>
  <rule name="co-authored-by">Do NOT add any Co-Authored-By trailer. Never add "Co-Authored-By: Claude" or similar.</rule>
  <rule name="trailers">Append these trailers at the end of the commit message body, separated by a blank line:
    AI-assisted: Claude Code
    On-behalf-of: @SAP christian.berendt@sap.com
    Signed-off-by: Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>
  </rule>
</git-identity>


OUTPUT ONLY THE COMMIT MESSAGE. No markdown, no explanation, no code fences.

FORMAT:
1. Subject: `type(CC-0114): concise summary of what was achieved` (max 72 chars)
2. Empty line
3. Body: Descriptive bullet points (each starting with "- ")
   - Each bullet describes ONE logical change in imperative mood
   - Describe WHAT was changed and WHY, in enough detail to understand the change
   - 5-20 bullets depending on scope — be thorough and detailed for large changes,
     so the message fully summarises everything the feature delivers
   - Group related changes by area (feature code, tests, refactors) into clear bullets
   - If the branch added work BEYOND the original feature scope (improvements found
     during manual review/testing), put those bullets under a final line `Additionally:`
     so they are explicitly marked as extra work, e.g.:
       Additionally:
       - Harden input validation discovered missing during review


EXAMPLE:
feat(CC-0114): add merge type choice and improve commit messages

- Add merge type choice dialog (squash vs regular) to ApproveButton
- Support merge_type parameter in approve endpoint for regular merges
- Improve Claude prompt to analyze diff instead of listing commit subjects
- Use feature title as commit subject instead of first commit message
